_comment: Replica of the dropbox.com homepage. Site-specific knowledge lives ONLY in
this file and app/ClientRuntime.tsx; scripts/** stay URL-agnostic.
Every key below is justified by THIS run's own capture — see the
underscore-prefixed notes for the evidence that was actually checked.
_captureMode: 'rendered', decided on a DOM-level probe of this run's capture rather than
left on 'auto': scrape/raw/index.static.html (the pre-JS response) contains
0 <video> elements while the rendered DOM contains 5. The hero + 3 product
videos are injected client-side, so 'static' would ship them as empty boxes.
Element counts alone would NOT have revealed this (static 593KB / rendered
710KB, img 78 vs 77) — assets must be judged as their own category.

_dropSelectors: NOTE: this list REPLACES the defaults in scripts/lib/config.mjs, so the
defaults are repeated verbatim here and the 4 site-specific entries are
appended at the end. Each site-specific entry and why:
part of the design; leaving it in bakes a consent bar into the page.
Expect it as permanent residue in `compare` (live still shows it).
iframe[src=about:blank] ..... empty runtime iframe with visibility:hidden.
source[type*=quicktime] ..... the 4 <source> siblings offering the same
videos as .mov (video/quicktime; codecs=hvc1). Every browser the
harness runs picks the .webm, and the hero .mov alone is 141MB, so
referencing them would force a 141MB file into public/ for an asset
that is never requested. The .webm siblings are kept.

_extraAssets: One entry: the favicon. This CORRECTS an earlier conclusion in this file.
https://dropbox.com/favicon.ico really is a 404 (curl, both www and the
apex redirect), which made it look like the site has no icon at all. It
A <head> link is not a DOM asset reference the scraper walks, so it never
entered scrape/asset-map.json; codegen's icon handling then dropped it for
having no local copy (see droppedIcons in scripts/codegen.mjs), leaving
generated/metadata.ts with no `icons` key. With no declared icon the
browser falls back to probing the origin root, which 404s and trips the
`console-errors` gate at iphone-se -- and unlike overflow/hiddenContent,
console errors have NO baseline path in scripts/viewport-check.mjs.
Listing the real URL here self-hosts it and lets codegen point metadata at
the local /assets copy: faithful to upstream AND no 404.
